input: arr contains n unique strictly increasing integers, 2 <= n <=1000, arr[0]=1, every later value prime, and all values <=30000. k is an integer in [1,n*(n-1)/2]. Integer inputs are plain int, excluding bool; list and string inputs are ordinary list/str values without subclasses. No concurrent mutation or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Size bounds do not guarantee available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: A fresh two-integer list [numerator value,denominator value] for the kth smallest fraction arr[i]/arr[j] over i<j. Fractions are compared exactly, not by rounded quotients. Distinct prime values plus 1 make the represented fractions distinct.
mutation_aliasing: All input values, caller containers and ordering remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state and separate calls share no mutable result state. The heap borrows arr read-only and owns fresh index-pair records. Pop/push changes only private heap storage. The result is a fresh pair of immutable input values and never aliases arr or an internal pair record.
numeric: Cross-products for ordering are <=30000^2=900000000, exact safe integers. No floating division is used. Heap lengths are <=n-1, rank <=499500, and doubled child indices are small. A deterministic index tie-break is included even though ties are excluded by the prime input contract.
complexity: O(n+k*log(n+1)) time and O(n+1) live auxiliary heap space. Bottom-up heap construction is O(n); each popped denominator stream advances its numerator once. O(n+k) constant-size pair records may be allocated across the call, but at most n-1 are retained in the heap. This k-sensitive algorithm does not claim subquadratic worst-case time when k is quadratic in n.

helpers.name: FractionHeap
helpers.contract: Fully included binary min-heap of (numerator index,denominator index) records, ordered by exact cross-products then indices. Construction includes one [0,j] record for each denominator and bottom-up sift-down. push sifts up; pop replaces the root with the last record and sifts down. It never modifies the borrowed value array.

The entire class, constructor, comparator, sift, push and pop methods are charged. Build O(n), push/pop O(log(n+1)), comparison O(1) on bounded values, live O(n), total record allocation O(n+k).
